note: Live-session recording of the screen scenes (series/tools/rec). prepare/teardown run on the laptop, not recorded; commands are typed and run for real. Screens that mix a terminal and a portal carry the second half in also[] (when = before/after the main part). Scenes read MG_LAB_ADMIN_UPN / MG_LAB_DOMAIN (set by prepare, derived from the signed-in labadmin).
prepare: Connect-MgGraph -Scopes Sites.Read.All, Sites.Manage.All, Group.ReadWrite.All, User.Read.All -NoWelcome  # owner signs in (browser)

function New-LabSite($name, $nick) { $g = (Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Uri "/v1.0/groups?`$filter=displayName eq '$name'").value | Select-Object -First 1; if (-not $g) { $g = Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Method POST -Uri /v1.0/groups -Body @{ displayName = $name; mailNickname = $nick; mailEnabled = $true; securityEnabled = $false; groupTypes = @('Unified'); 'owners@odata.bind' = @("https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/$((Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Uri /v1.0/me).id)") } }; $d = $null; for ($i = 0; $i -lt 30 -and -not $d; $i++) { Start-Sleep -Seconds 10; try { $d = Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Uri "/v1.0/groups/$($g.id)/sites/root/drive" } catch {} }; [pscustomobject]@{ Group = $g; Drive = $d } }
# team site MG Lab Forms: labadmin owner; alex.demo, sam.demo and jordan.demo members (they only answer the form)

$site = New-LabSite 'MG Lab Forms' 'mg-lab-forms'; foreach ($u in 'alex.demo', 'sam.demo', 'jordan.demo') { try { Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Method POST -Uri "/v1.0/groups/$($site.Group.id)/members/`$ref" -Body @{ '@odata.id' = "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/$(Get-LabUserId $u)" } } catch {} }
./src/Invoke-FormsData.ps1 -SpecFile ./src/form.lab.json -Validate   # off-camera dry run; do not provision yet

steps: Open the 'MG Lab Forms' site > Site contents > 'M365 Apps Pulse Responses'
Show the columns: ResponseId required (List settings > column > 'Enforce unique values'), the Rating minimum and maximum, the Department choices
If Graph rejected a property in the terminal, show the real error and fix the module

screens.name: flow
steps: Forms: new form 'Microsoft 365 Apps rollout pulse' with the six questions of form.json, same wording (Department as Choice, Rating as Rating or Choice 1 to 5, apps as Choice with Multiple answers, Comment as long text, Yes/No as Choice, date as Date)
Settings: only people in my organization can respond; Record name on
Show the editor with the six questions
Terminal (see also[]) prints the mapping table with ./Invoke-FormsData.ps1 -FlowMap; keep it next to the designer
Power Automate, environment DEV: new automated cloud flow 'MG Lab - Forms to SharePoint': trigger Microsoft Forms > When a new response is submitted (select the form)
Action Get response details (Form Id, Response Id from the trigger); action SharePoint > Create item (the MG Lab Forms site, the new list)
Fill the columns from the FlowMap table; Title = concat('Response ', <Response Id>); record how the multi-select answer arrives and whether an expression such as join is needed
Save and turn the flow on; show the designer
make.powerautomate.com, environment DEV: build and save the flow described above

screens.name: analyze
screens.account: alex.demo, sam.demo and jordan.demo in three separate private windows
steps: Open the form link in each private window and submit for real: different departments and ratings; at least one low rating without a comment and one multi-select with two apps
Power Automate > My flows > the flow > run history: the runs succeeded (wait a few minutes; if a run failed show the real error and fix the flow)
SharePoint: Site contents > the list shows the rows
Run the analysis in the terminal (see also[]); expect LowRatingNoComment, everything else only if it really happens
Real gap, no faking: Forms > Responses: delete one response, run the analysis again: ResponseIdGap
Optional real test: turn the flow off, submit once, turn it on, analyze again; say only what you observe about back-filling

teardown: foreach ($g in (Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Uri "/v1.0/groups?`$filter=displayName eq 'MG Lab Forms'").value) { Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Method DELETE -Uri "/v1.0/groups/$($g.id)" }   # the team site and its list go with the group

Start-Sleep -Seconds 30; foreach ($g in (Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Uri "/v1.0/directory/deletedItems/microsoft.graph.group?`$filter=displayName eq 'MG Lab Forms'").value) { Invoke-MgGraphRequest -Method DELETE -Uri "/v1.0/directory/deletedItems/$($g.id)" }
